issue_context.summary: Investigate stale extension query updates overwriting newer typed input
inferences: The proposed mechanism is provisional and is not an executed runtime result or evidence that the old report is fixed.
known_information: The0.102.3001report states that text disappears while first-load extension results arrive, without the reporter pressing Backspace.

Downloaded and inspected the supplied23.57second recording: the Colors page has rapidly changing typed queries and delayed/mismatched result states. The recording has no key-event overlay, so the no-Backspace assertion remains reporter evidence.

Exact current-main ListViewModel serializes outgoing dynamic SearchText updates but also accepts model SearchText property updates. SearchBar.Page_PropertyChanged then assigns differing list.SearchText into FilterBox.Text and moves the caret.
That establishes a real incoming/outgoing synchronization boundary, not proof whether this extension emits stale values or the host incorrectly orders them.
issue_context.analysis: An older extension SearchText notification may overwrite a later user edit during asynchronous loading. Correlate user-edit sequence, provider request/result and incoming property notification before deciding whether host freshness tracking or extension behavior needs correction. Preserve intentional provider-driven query replacement.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report/empty discussion and inspected twelve evenly spaced full-frame samples from the supplied video.
Read immutable origin/main ListViewModel.cs and SearchBar.xaml.cs, rather than relying on the dirty shared checkout versions. No provider runtime trace or fixed build is claimed.

fix_assessment.rationale: An observable failure is reported and a specific investigation boundary is identified. The proposed direction remains conditional on controlled reproduction.

actions.label: Reproduce Command Palette dynamic query input behavior

prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.
steps: Use the shown Colors extension and a test dynamic provider with controlled first-query latency; type successive distinct queries while the first result is pending.
Record ordered user edits, outgoing SearchText assignments, result completion and incoming SearchText notifications; distinguish result-list lag from actual textbox rollback.
Complete old requests out of order and verify whether stale notifications replace the latest text; separately exercise intentional query reset, page navigation and provider-driven replacement.
reproduce.expected: Late results or stale query echoes must not erase a newer user edit; intentional provider-driven query replacements and navigation must continue to work.
